observations.summary: 9 out of 10 people in the US get tap water from a public water system; utilities must meet EPA standards and notify customers of violations; private well owners are responsible for their water's safety.
observations.inference_limit: National context; not a statement about a specific Santa Cruz County system.

observations.summary: Community water systems publish annual Consumer Confidence Reports; consumers can find their local report.

Test private wells annually for total coliform bacteria, nitrates, total dissolved solids and pH; test after flooding, land disturbance, well repairs or a change in odor, color or taste; symptom to test table (stains: iron, copper, manganese; scale: hardness; taste or smell: hydrogen sulfide, corrosion, metals; lead plumbing: pH, lead, copper; cloudy or colored: color, detergents); use certified labs.
observations.inference_limit: General guidance; not a local code requirement.

observations.summary: Point of use RO can remove lead, VOCs, PFAS, arsenic, bacteria and viruses; typical units reject 5+ gallons per gallon treated, inefficient up to 10; WaterSense labeled max 2.3; saves over 3,100 gallons per year on average; EPA does not promote RO for every application.
observations.inference_limit: Product category guidance; not a Wade product claim.

observations.summary: County EH: softener brine can damage tank bacteria, clog the leach field and increase hydraulic load; best is no softener or exchange tank; discharge brine to a separate drywell or subsurface system; septic discharge highly discouraged; ground discharge prohibited; sewer properties discharge to sewer.

LAMP Appendix A sewage ordinance: discharge from water softeners, drinking water filters, swimming pool filter backwash and other non-domestic wastewater shall not be discharged to the septic system (raised by Codex review citing SCCC 7.38.150(A)(5)).
observations.inference_limit: Ordinance text as published by County EH; homeowners should confirm current requirements with EH.
